To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a demand curve approach to capacity markets will lower consumer prices and increase the reliability of supply.

a demand curve approach is more effective than the present fixed requirement in reducing the cost of capacity for consumers, while providing a stable revenue stream to generators and a reduced incentive for over-investment in generation.
a sloped demand-curve-based capacity market is likely to result in lower consumer costs than the present fixed requirement approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a proposed change from a fixed requirement to a demand curve-based capacity market.
the effects of a demand curve-based capacity market on consumer costs.

the design of an efficient market to meet capacity obligations in a manner that provides incentives to construct new generating capacity, while at the same time providing incentives to operate existing generating capacity in the most efficient manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PJM Reliability Price Model is a significant advance in the development of capacity markets.
a demand curve-based capacity market is likely to result in lower consumer costs and higher generator profits.
the demand curve-based capacity market is superior to the fixed capacity requirement for all of the reasons stated above, and the cost savings are substantial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PJM proposal to replace the existing fixed ICAP requirement with a demand curve approach is a step in the right direction.
demand curves are superior to fixed requirements for both consumers and generators.
demand curves are superior to the present fixed capacity requirement for the PJM region.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed PJM demand curve approach is a significant improvement over the present fixed requirement, but that there are significant uncertainties concerning the effects upon generator behavior, which could result in a different outcome than the one predicted by our representative agent model.

the demand curve-based approach to capacity obligations is a significant improvement over the existing fixed capacity obligation in the PJM market, and the demand curve approach is likely to be more cost-effective than the present approach in most markets.
the demand curve-based capacity market is an improvement over the present system in the PJM.
